The lower bound of SET_PACK_CELLS is a validity bound: the settings table says its ranges are the physical ones, 'a pack cannot have zero cells' (settings.c:34-35). The lowest counts of ADBMS6948 and LTC6813 are not read here: www.analog.com refuses requests after about 15 (Research.md prerequisite 2), and finding the figure is P2's task.

The load is the motor current: up to 150 A continuous on the onboard path (F2, IOBoard.md:420), and above 150 A to 300 A and more on the external path (Research.md:62). questions.question: What is the lowest cell count, in cells, of an ESC pack that the cell monitor reads on its balance lead? The page gives 1 to 16 cells. F15 gives only the top, 16 cells. The 1 is the lower bound of SET_PACK_CELLS, which the settings table sets as a physical limit ('a pack cannot have zero cells').
questions.why: P2 cannot keep or drop a monitor by its lowest cell count. BQ76952 reads 3 to 16 cells and BQ76942 3 to 10 (ti.com, read 2026-09-28T10:26Z). A monitor that takes its supply from the stack needs a stack voltage that a 1-cell or 2-cell pack may not reach.
questions.for_quantity: lowest cell count of the ESC pack on the balance lead

questions.question: What resolution, in mV, does each cell voltage reading need? The screen prints each cell to 0.01 V, the pack mean to 0.001 V and the spread in whole mV. The per-cell resistance under load divides a cell's voltage change by the current change, so this resolution also bounds the resistance.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the resolution per cell as not stated (R9). Without it P2 cannot drop a monitor whose converter is too coarse.

questions.question: What largest error, in mV, may each cell voltage reading have under load, and over which ambient temperature range, in °C? The spread verdict switches at 30 mV and 60 mV between two cells (shared/ui/battery_screen.c:46-47).
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the accuracy per cell as not stated (R9). The tree states the board's ambient range only for the monostable's window, 0 to 50 °C (IOBoard.md:184). P2 cannot check a datasheet's total measurement error without the figure and its temperature range.

questions.question: What is the lowest cell voltage, in V, that the cell monitor reads within that error? F15 sets the top at 4.2 V a cell. The ESC pack's chemistry and discharge floor are not stated.
questions.why: A datasheet states its cell error over a limited input range. P2 cannot check that range against the cells the bench reads.

questions.question: How often, in ms, does the cell monitor read every cell of a 16-cell pack? The coprocessor samples the bench numbers every 20 ms (IOBoard.md:431). No rate is stated for the cells.
questions.why: P2 cannot check a monitor's conversion time for 16 cells, or its bus traffic, against a rate that is not stated.

questions.question: What largest time, in µs, may separate the first and the last cell sample of one reading of the pack? The spread is measured under load (IOBoard.md:437), where each cell's voltage follows the ESC's current.
questions.why: A monitor that converts the cells one after another over milliseconds reads each cell at a different current, and shows a spread the pack does not have. P2 cannot choose between simultaneous and sequential conversion without this figure.

questions.question: What largest time, in µs, may separate a cell voltage sample from the motor current sample it is paired with for the per-cell resistance under load? The current comes from the INA238 (R8).
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists how the cell samples align with the current as not stated (R9). P2 cannot qualify a monitor's trigger or timestamp against the INA238's conversion without it.

questions.question: What voltage, in V, must the cell monitor's balance-lead input be rated for, above the 67.2 V of F15? Round 2 selects the overvoltage protection on the balance-lead connector (Research.md:28), which clamps under that rating. No line places the balance lead behind R3's input protection on the ESC pack's power path.
questions.why: P2 cannot drop a monitor whose absolute maximum sits too close to 67.2 V for a clamp to fit under it. P5's ESC pack node clamp check needs the figure.

questions.question: What largest voltage, in V, may stand between the ESC pack's negative at the balance lead and the IO board's ground during a motor test? If the cell monitor is isolated from the RP2354B instead, what isolation voltage, in V? The ESC pack's return reaches the star point by its own lead (testbench/WIRING.md:37-39). Which side of the motor supply the shunts sit on is not stated (IOBoard.md:469). The isolation between the 150 A path and the 3.3 V I²C bus is not defined (IOBoard.md:497).
questions.why: Without the offset or the isolation voltage, P2 cannot choose between a monitor on the board's ground, read directly over I²C or SPI, and one behind an isolated interface, or qualify either.

questions.question: What largest current, in µA, may the cell monitor draw from any one pin of the ESC pack's balance lead, with the IO board powered and with it unpowered? An uneven draw across the pins discharges the cells unevenly and opens the spread the screen judges.
questions.why: A monitor that takes its supply from the top of the stack draws from the upper pins. P2 cannot qualify a monitor's supply and input currents without a limit.

questions.question: What voltages, in V, must the balance-lead input survive from a mis-plugged lead: the largest reverse voltage on any pin against the lead's lowest pin, and the largest voltage between two adjacent pins? A lead plugged in reversed, or shifted by one pin, puts these voltages on the input.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the protection against a mis-plugged lead as not stated (R9). P2 cannot check a monitor's absolute maximum ratings on its cell inputs against mis-plug cases that are not stated.

questions.question: How many connectors, of how many cells each, carry the ESC pack's balance lead to the IO board? A 16-cell pack's balance lead can arrive as one lead or as several. A lead plugged in without the others leaves inputs open.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the balance-lead connector sizes as not stated (R9). Round 2 selects the connector part (Research.md:28). Without the arrangement, P2 cannot check which inputs a monitor sees open, or whether it survives the leads plugged in any order.

questions.question: May a jumper or an adapter lead set the cell count at the balance-lead input? Answer yes or no, and if yes, the number of positions. With no setting, a pack of any count from the lowest to 16 cells plugs in with no change on the board.
questions.why: Some monitors need unused cell inputs shorted, or take their supply from the top cell. They read a smaller pack only through such a setting. P2 cannot keep or drop them without the answer.
